name: Agent CLI config
description: Installs coding-agent CLIs at build time — the Claude Code CLI, and optionally the GitHub Copilot CLI, the pi coding agent CLI, the Herdr terminal multiplexer and the agent-browser browser-automation CLI, with room for more to join the same install-guard shape later — and at create time optionally links one fixed seed directory into ~/.claude (opt-in, see claudeSeed), points ~/.config/herdr at a second fixed seed directory, and installs any declared pi packages and Herdr plugins. The pi/Herdr install is deliberately at create time, not build time, even though this Feature validates those two options at build time: neither ~/.pi nor ~/.config/herdr is a mount, so either way whatever gets installed is container-local and gone on the next full rebuild — but a build-time install sits inside a Docker RUN layer, which Docker's build cache can silently keep serving stale (an unchanged option value on a plain "Rebuild Container" skips re-running the layer, so an upstream plugin's moved default branch is never re-fetched); a create-time install has no layer to go stale, so a plain rebuild always re-resolves each source's current tip. Also optionally installs agent-browser's Chrome for Testing build plus the Linux system libraries it needs, since ~/.agent-browser is not a mount either. No path options: the two seeds are always /usr/local/share/devc-features/agents/claude-seed and .../herdr-seed, the one thing a consumer decides is what to bind-mount onto either. The claude-seed half is off by default — the declared ~/.claude volume already captures all of Claude Code's state on its own — and the herdr-seed half is unconditional, because ~/.config/herdr is not a mount and there is nothing there for a flag to protect. Declares its own per-devcontainer ~/.claude volume, keyed on ${devcontainerId}, so persistence needs no mount line in the consumer's config; the target is necessarily the literal /home/vscode/.claude, because no substitution variable names the remote user's home, and post-create.sh warns when that is not this user's home. Also points CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at the literal /home/vscode/.claude — the same literal, for the same reason, as the declared volume's target — so Claude Code writes .claude.json inside the volume itself rather than beside it as ~/.claude.json, and post-create.sh no longer has to relocate that file.

installClaudeCli.description: Install the Claude Code CLI at build time, as the remote user, into ~/.local/bin — not shadowed by the ~/.claude volume mounted at create time, and writable by that user afterwards (`claude update` etc.). Idempotent: a rebuild does not re-download when the binary is already there.

installCopilotCli.description: Install the GitHub Copilot CLI at build time, same shape as installClaudeCli. Defaults false: each agent CLI stays opt-in on its own, so enabling this Feature for Claude does not silently install a second vendor's CLI too.

installPiCli.description: Install the pi coding agent CLI at build time, same shape as installClaudeCli. Defaults false: each agent CLI stays opt-in on its own, so enabling this Feature for Claude does not silently install a third vendor's CLI too. Unlike the other two, pi installs itself with npm, so this option requires Node.js 22.19.0 or newer and npm in the image — add a node Feature alongside this one (installsAfter already orders this Feature behind it). The binary lands in ~/.local/bin beside claude and copilot, not in the active nvm node version's directory.

installHerdr.description: Install the Herdr terminal multiplexer at build time, same shape as installClaudeCli. Defaults false: each tool stays opt-in on its own, so enabling this Feature for Claude does not silently install another vendor's tool too. Ships a static binary — no Node.js prerequisite. Herdr's config and plugin state (~/.config/herdr, ~/.local/state/herdr) are not mounts, so whatever they hold is container-local — a Herdr session does not outlive its container, and neither do plugins installed via herdrPlugins (which reinstalls fresh on every container create, not just once at build — see herdrPlugins' own description).

piPackages.description: Comma-separated pi package sources, e.g. 'npm:@andrewjacop/pi-herdr,git:github.com/bmingles/pi-dev-extensions@main'. Requires installPiCli — a non-empty value with installPiCli false fails the build, checked at build time even though the actual install is not. Empty (the default) installs nothing. Each entry is passed to `pi install <entry>` as-is; pi accepts npm:, git:, https://, ssh:// and local-path sources, and this option does not parse or validate the form. Installed at container CREATE time (every container creation, including a plain "Rebuild Container"), not build time — deliberately: ~/.pi is not a mount, so a build-time install would sit inside a Docker RUN layer, and Docker's build cache can serve that layer's stale result on a rebuild whose option value did not change, even though a `git:` (or `npm:`-latest) source's upstream tip moved since. A create-time install has no layer to go stale — it re-resolves each source's current tip on every rebuild, with nothing to pin and no --no-cache needed. A volume later mounted at ~/.pi shadows everything this option installed, the same footgun this Feature already documents for ~/.claude. A failed entry at create time warns and continues rather than failing container creation — unlike a failed build, a failed container creation would leave you without a container to open at all.

herdrPlugins.description: Comma-separated Herdr plugins, in GitHub shorthand only (owner/repo[/subdir]), e.g. 'bmingles/herdr-plugins/agent-caffeinate'. Requires installHerdr — a non-empty value with installHerdr false fails the build, checked at build time even though the actual install is not. Empty (the default) installs nothing. Installed with `herdr plugin install <entry> --yes`; needs git and network. Installed at container CREATE time (every container creation, including a plain "Rebuild Container"), not build time — deliberately: plugin registration is global to the user, not per session, so *where* it runs was always free to be create time rather than build time, and create time is what makes a rebuild reliably pick up wherever the plugin's default branch points now, rather than whatever commit Docker's build cache happened to keep from the layer's last real execution (see this Feature's own top-level description). A plugin whose min_herdr_version exceeds the installed Herdr version, or any other failed entry, warns and continues at create time rather than failing container creation — unlike the old build-time behavior, a failed container creation would leave you without a container to open at all.

installAgentBrowser.description: Install the agent-browser CLI at build time, same shape as installClaudeCli. Defaults false: each tool stays opt-in on its own. Installs with npm, so — like installPiCli — it requires Node.js and npm in the image; add a node Feature alongside this one (installsAfter already orders this Feature behind it). Unlike pi, what lands on PATH is a native binary rather than a node script, so the container's active Node version does not affect running it.

agentBrowserChrome.description: What `agent-browser install` does at build time. 'with-deps' also apt-installs the ~36 shared libraries and fonts Chrome needs on Linux; 'browser-only' downloads Chrome and skips them; 'none' installs no browser at all — the right value when you drive a remote browser over --cdp or a cloud provider. Read only when installAgentBrowser is true, and silently ignored otherwise — this option is not a second way to turn the CLI on. Chrome for Testing is about 390 MB on disk and lands in ~/.agent-browser, which is not a mount.

claudeSeed.description: Link every top-level file from this Feature's fixed seed directory (/usr/local/share/devc-features/agents/claude-seed) into ~/.claude at container create time. Defaults false: the declared ~/.claude volume already captures all of Claude Code's state on its own, and with nothing bind-mounted onto the seed path there is nothing to link anyway. Turn it on when you bind-mount your own host config directory onto that seed path and want its files to appear in ~/.claude as live symlinks. The seed never overwrites a real file — it only creates links and replaces its own — so a name already present in ~/.claude is skipped with a warning. If ~/.claude is itself a bind mount of a host directory, note that the links point at a container path and will look broken when you open that directory on the host. Directories in the seed are ignored by design: something else may have mounted per-skill binds under ~/.claude/skills/.
